summary: Unmarked nominal stimuli with Preterit Intransitive are directly attested: əšma (MAC Murder in Kfarze, Interview with Numan/40), a human NP (PrS 61/80; 96/289), u mawto (PrS 72/38), u dalqayḏa (63/192), u lġono (95/231), i zəndaniyayo (96/178), u msarqo (113/159). These prevent a categorical claim that qaṭəl avoids nominal stimuli.
JTM 1.1/63 ṭaʕət mede is a clear indefinite-stimulus candidate, whereas its second token lies in a relative clause. The existing 62/343 example already has the unmarked action nominal u=mḥoyayḏi.

Separate resumed topics from unresumed objects: JL 14.8/20 fronted good deed is resumed by -la; 5/6 days by -lən. 57/210 haṯe and MAC Besim History of Bsorino/55 melody may be detached topics; MAC Besim Martyrdom of Maferyono/25 gives a clearer postverbal melody NP.

115/190 has an l-marked human stimulus plus suffix, while many Infectum examples have unmarked nominal, pronominal, omitted or clausal stimuli. A quantitative frequency claim cannot be inferred from these selected readings alone.
Preterit-wa ṭaʕinowo/ṭaʕiwayno and Infinitiv ṭʕoyo/təṭʕiyo fill missing boxes. In III the experiencer becomes the affected object, while the forgotten stimulus can be omitted.

Reflexive ruḥ- and reciprocal ḥḏoḏe uses express absorption in enjoyment; the reflexive construction is already noted, so do not create another numbered sense or duplicate idiom. Reciprocal 66/264 needs checking against the edition's expanded translation.

Existing 5/6 has fifteen in Turoyo but the supplied edition German has fourteen; the stored entry wording is not silently rewritten. At Hors 1/27 the reader's plural experiencer conflicts with singular narrator discourse and German ich; ṭaʕinanne may instead be 1sg plus plural stimulus. Segmentation requires checking.

Jan material here combines transcribed interviews and authored political discussion; it is not uniformly literary prose. Current failed recall is repeatedly expressed by Preterit Intransitive ṭaʕino/ṭaʕyono; Infectum covers recurrent forgetting and prospective injunctions.

Separate unresumed əšme after ṭaʕino from fronted or doubled stimuli with -le/-la: Jan 1.44/1905, 2.5/1397, 2.32/5300 and 3.34/955. Jan 2.35/5655 kul mede follows mbadelan, so its scope over ṭaʕina is uncertain.
III maṭʕəlelanne at Jan 1.33/1413 makes u zawno the causer; compare institutional policy with maṭʕi at Jan 4.I/473. Causer and experiencer differ from I experiencer-subject constructions.
The reader labels ṭaʕətle at Jan 2.35/5507 Infectum, but the a-vowel form agrees with the other Preterit Intransitive second-person tokens. No new box or sense follows.

summary: Round 1 Detransitive sense 1 vergessen werden is supported by plural kməṭʕoyi, masculine kməṭʕe and feminine kməṭʕoyo; no new sense. Negated forms often imply inability to forget in context, without an overt modal.

Bare postverbal nominal stimuli recur with Preterit Intransitive across Išoʕ, Brahim, Aziz and Maḥbe; clear cases include am masayəlani, i turəke and əšme/əšmayye. This confirms round 1 rather than introducing a construction.

Inanimate experiencer expressions meḥi and i yaminayḏan extend participant choice within forgetting. The latter is in an explicitly quoted conditional/curse and cannot alone establish ordinary prose valency.
